hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to a prominent, dark-colored object or region—typically jet black, charcoal grey, or deep brown—contrasted against a bright, desaturated background of white, pale beige, light gray, or dry straw yellow. The activating feature often presents as a solid, high-contrast silhouette or mass, such as the body of a black animal (dog, ostrich, bear), a dark electronic screen, or a deep shadowed cavity. The neuron is invariant to the specific identity of the object, its texture (fur, feathers, plastic), and the lighting conditions, as long as the distinct dark-on-light polarity is preserved. The activating feature typically occupies 20–50% of the image area and is centered or situated in the lower half of the frame.
